response: The Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka are 14 separate, significantly detailed inscriptions — among the earliest dated rock inscriptions of any Indian monarch. They are preceded chronologically by the Minor Rock Edicts. They belong to a larger collection of more than thirty inscriptions attributed to Emperor Ashoka of the Mauryan Empire, who ruled most of the Indian subcontinent from 268 to 232 BCE. The edicts were carved on in-situ rocks or engraved on pillars erected throughout the empire, and they carry teachings of the Buddha.
